translit: ātmaiva hyātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
theme: You are your own best friend
hindi: मनुष्य को अपने द्वारा स्वयं को ऊपर उठाना चाहिए, स्वयं को नीचे नहीं गिराना चाहिए। क्योंकि मनुष्य स्वयं ही अपना मित्र है और स्वयं ही अपना शत्रु।
english: Lift yourself up by your own effort; never let yourself sink down. For you alone are your own friend, and you alone are your own enemy.
deeper: The word atma appears again and again in this verse, with layers of meaning: your higher self — your wise, steady mind — must lift your lower self — your lazy, scared or angry side.
The same mind can build you or break you. In the next verse (6.6) Krishna says: for one who has won over the mind, it is the best friend; for one who hasn’t, it behaves like an enemy.

Teachers, parents and God can show the way and support you — but nobody can do your push-ups for you. Thoughts like “I’m useless” or “I can never do it” are the mind acting as an enemy. Thoughts like “I’m still learning” are the mind acting as a friend.
background: Chapter 6 is called Dhyana Yoga — the yoga of meditation. Krishna has explained that true renunciation is not running away from duties, but giving up selfish desire (6.1–2).
He describes how a person climbs towards yoga: first through good action, then through inner calm (6.3–4). And now he gives the key: this climb is something only you can do for yourself.
lessons: Talk to yourself like a good friend would.
Encourage, don’t insult — your mind is listening.
Discipline is a form of self-love.
Saying “no” to small temptations is saying “yes” to your future.
Take the first small step yourself; help follows effort.
Change one tiny daily choice and you change yourself.
No fall is final while you are willing to stand up.
examples: The alarm rings and your mind says, “Just five more minutes.” Here the mind is acting as an enemy. Getting up is making it your friend.
Instead of “I’m bad at maths,” Neel started saying, “I’m still learning maths.” Slowly, his fear faded.
In the middle of homework, Tanya felt like opening a game. She put her phone in another room — she lifted herself up.
When someone teased her, Kriti started feeling worthless. Then she wrote down three good things about herself and smiled.
Aditya had a habit of eating chips every day. He decided by himself: only on Sundays. Nobody forced him.
Saumya started reading just 10 pages a day. In one year, she finished 15 books!
Before speaking at the school assembly, Vivaan’s hands were shaking. He told himself, “I can do this” — and he did.
Kabir broke a window pane. Instead of hiding it, he told the truth. By being honest, he rose in his own eyes.

story.title: Eklavya’s Determination
paras: Eklavya, a boy who lived in the forest, dreamed of becoming a great archer. He went to Guru Dronacharya to learn, but the guru refused to accept him as a student.
Anyone else might have said, “My luck is bad,” and given up. But Eklavya did not let himself sink.
He made a clay statue of Guru Dronacharya in the forest, bowed to it, and began practising from morning till evening. Sun or rain, he didn’t stop for a single day.
Slowly his aim became so perfect that one day he filled a barking dog’s mouth with arrows without hurting it at all. When Arjuna and Dronacharya saw this, even they were amazed.
story.moral: Lesson: Even when a door is closed, you can build your own path. Your own mind can become your greatest friend.

quiz.q: According to this verse, who is our best friend?
quiz.x: “Ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhuḥ” — you alone are your own friend.

o: By practising alone before a clay statue of his guru
quiz.x: Even after being refused, he lifted himself through his own dedication.

quiz.q: A thought comes: “I can never do well.” According to the Gita, what is this?
o: The mind acting as a friend
The mind acting as an enemy
quiz.x: A thought that pulls you down makes the mind your enemy.

reel.hook: Who is your best friend? The answer may surprise you.
reel.lesson: Talk to yourself like a good friend would.
reel.caption:
Lift yourself up 🧗
You can be your own best friend — or your own enemy.
